Shared Normal Geometry for Charge and Sector Frames

Updated October 9, 2026

The Common Geometric Question

The same ordinary spatial normal bundle can constrain charge representations, polarization, intermediate sector embeddings and possible contact tensors. The construction below makes that reuse explicit. It establishes geometric identities and conditional dimension criteria; it does not identify occupied particle states or a physical electric interaction.

Throughout, a normal vector is a direction in the containing spatial manifold. Spinor components and coefficient-ray spaces describe fields at a point. They are not additional physical sectors. The spatial-depth module specifies the tangent Clifford compatibility needed for each sector operator.

The same polynomial basis, determinant line and complete field carrier constrain all three.

The normal charge, rotation and oriented-volume note adds an exact character comparison and a geometric reading of the charge weights. The rank-three even carrier alone has a nonzero cubic trace among m≥2m\ge2m≥2; its full Clifford completion cancels that trace. Every rank-three chiral polarization determines an orthogonal normal complex structure, whereas an explicit fixed-charge state at every higher rank can fail that property. Definite-grade charge weights measure relative normal rotation alignment with the existing determinant-branch shift. Correlated frame tensors also show that complete oriented volume is not determined by their scalar norm. These are conditional consequences of the same normal construction; they do not select physical particle charge or a new interaction coefficient.

21. Interpretation And Reproduction

These results provide a conditional normal-dimension discriminator and explicit common geometric realizations. They also constrain how charge, polarization and sector projections can coexist. They do not establish the previously proposed preference at four of the six assigned particle depths. The sector-case paper places this evidence beside the separately scoped mass comparisons.

The single exact checker and recorded results verify representation signs, projectors, covariant maps, sharp-bound witnesses, curvature and competing examples. The all-dimension and global conclusions also depend on the proofs above; a check count is not a count of independent empirical predictions. No particle evolution is required for these tests.
